commands.command: openclaw plugins update/install fails with "npm view produced incomplete package metadata" on npm 12 environment openclaw: 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4) node: v26.4.0 npm: 12.0.1 (fails) / 10.9.8 (works) os: cachyos linux, kernel 7.1.3-2-cachyos-server-lto (x86_64) registry: reproduced on both registry.npmjs.org and registry.npmmirror.com summary on npm 12, every openclaw plugins update --all and plugin install reports npm view produced incomplete package metadata and the operation fails. downgrading npm to v10 resolves it completely. the failure is not network/registry/package-existence related — all official plugins (discord, slack, email, longcat, wecom, etc.) resolve fine on npm 10 and via direct npm view on npm 12. steps to reproduce have npm 12.x installed (npm --version → 12.x) run openclaw plugins update --all or openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" observed behavior could not check discord before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata could not check email before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... failed to update discord: npm view produced incomplete package metadata failed to update email: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... for a direct install, the package tarball downloads and extracts successfully, but then: downloading @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin… extracting .../tencent-weixin-openclaw-weixin-2.4.6.tgz… npm view produced incomplete package metadata expected behavior plugin metadata check succeeds and the plugin installs / updates normally. root cause (analysis) openclaw's install/update flow calls: npm view <spec> name version dist.integrity dist.shasum openclaw --json --before=<now> and then requires the parsed result to contain name + version (see dist/install-source-utils-*.js, resolvenpmspecmetadata): const metadata = normalizenpmviewmetadata(json.parse(res.stdout.trim())); if (!metadata?.name || !metadata.version) return { ok:false, error:"npm view produced incomplete package metadata" }; on npm 12 the npm view --json output format / field shape differs from what this parser expects, so the guard trips even though the package exists and the tarball downloads fine. on npm 10 the same call returns the expected shape and everything works. evidence direct npm view @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin version on npm 12 → 2.4.6 (package exists, network fine) same npm view ... --json --before=... shape is what openclaw invokes; parse guard fails on npm 12 after npm install -g npm@10:and openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" → installed plugin: openclaw-weixin workaround downgrade npm to v10: npm install -g npm@10 then restart the gateway (systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway.service). suggested fix make resolvenpmspecmetadata tolerant of the npm 12 --json output shape (e.g. handle array vs object, and don't require the openclaw field for the existence/version check), or pin a known-good npm version range for the metadata check.
commands.freeform_prompt: openclaw plugins update/install fails with "npm view produced incomplete package metadata" on npm 12 Environment OpenClaw: 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4) Node: v26.4.0 npm: 12.0.1 (fails) / 10.9.8 (works) OS: CachyOS Linux, kernel 7.1.3-2-cachyos-server-lto (x86_64) Registry: reproduced on both registry.npmjs.org and registry.npmmirror.com Summary On npm 12, every openclaw plugins update --all and plugin install reports npm view produced incomplete package metadata and the operation fails. Downgrading npm to v10 resolves it completely. The failure is not network/registry/package-existence related — all official plugins (discord, slack, email, longcat, wecom, etc.) resolve fine on npm 10 and via direct npm view on npm 12. Steps to reproduce Have npm 12.x installed (npm --version → 12.x) Run openclaw plugins update --all or openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" Observed behavior Could not check discord before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata Could not check email before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... Failed to update discord: npm view produced incomplete package metadata Failed to update email: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... For a direct install, the package tarball downloads and extracts successfully, but then: Downloading @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin… Extracting .../tencent-weixin-openclaw-weixin-2.4.6.tgz… npm view produced incomplete package metadata Expected behavior Plugin metadata check succeeds and the plugin installs / updates normally. Root cause (analysis) OpenClaw's install/update flow calls: npm view <spec> name version dist.integrity dist.shasum openclaw --json --before=<now> and then requires the parsed result to contain name + version (see dist/install-source-utils-*.js, resolveNpmSpecMetadata): const metadata = normalizeNpmViewMetadata(JSON.parse(res.stdout.trim())); if (!metadata?.name || !metadata.version) return { ok:false, error:"npm view produced incomplete package metadata" }; On npm 12 the npm view --json output format / field shape differs from what this parser expects, so the guard trips even though the package exists and the tarball downloads fine. On npm 10 the same call returns the expected shape and everything works. Evidence Direct npm view @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin version on npm 12 → 2.4.6 (package exists, network fine) Same npm view ... --json --before=... shape is what OpenClaw invokes; parse guard fails on npm 12 After npm install -g npm@10:and openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" → Installed plugin: openclaw-weixin Workaround Downgrade npm to v10: npm install -g npm@10 Then restart the gateway (systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway.service). Suggested fix Make resolveNpmSpecMetadata tolerant of the npm 12 --json output shape (e.g. handle array vs object, and don't require the openclaw field for the existence/version check), or pin a known-good npm version range for the metadata check.

target.title: [Bug]: plugin metadata conflict can block gateway startup, and plugin repair/reinstall can silently drop plugin config/allowlist causing state drift
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On macOS, upgrading an existing npm/Homebrew-style OpenClaw install to `2026.7.1` can leave external plugins in a split-brain state:

1. a legacy plugin install metadata conflict prevents startup migrations from completing, so the gateway refuses readiness
2. `openclaw doctor --fix` does **not** clear it
3. after manual uninstall/reinstall of the conflicting plugin, the gateway can recover, but other external plugins may still have stale install/index state
4. during follow-up repair, a working plugin can silently lose its config entry / allowlist entry / API-key subtree, so the plugin is physically installed and partially loaded, but the capability is unusable until config is manually restored
5. even after successful recovery and a real successful capability call, some status surfaces still report old version drift

This leaves the system operational only after manual intervention across multiple layers (`plugins.entries.*`, `plugins.allow`, plugin reinstall, gateway restart), and the built-in repair flow does not converge state automatically.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a long-lived macOS install with external plugins already configured.

Environment before upgrade:
- OpenClaw `2026.6.11`
- macOS arm64
- Homebrew global install under `/opt/homebrew`
- external plugins present: `openclaw-weixin`, `@openclaw/deepseek-provider`, `@openclaw/tavily-plugin`
- web search configured to use `tavily`
- Tavily API key stored under plugin config

Upgrade flow:

1. Upgrade OpenClaw core to `2026.7.1`
2. Ensure Node is compatible (`v24.18.0` in this repro)
3. Run:
   - `openclaw gateway install`
   - `openclaw gateway start`
4. Observe gateway never becomes ready
5. `openclaw gateway status --deep` shows service loaded/running or restarting, but probe fails / port not truly ready
6. Logs show:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

7. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`
8. Observe the same plugin install metadata conflict remains; gateway still not ready
9. Manually force-uninstall and reinstall the conflicting plugin:
   - `openclaw plugins uninstall openclaw-weixin --force`
   - `openclaw plugins install @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin`
   - `openclaw plugins registry --refresh`
   - `openclaw gateway restart`
10. Gateway finally becomes healthy
11. Now inspect other external plugins (`deepseek`, `tavily`): installed files are present on disk, but status/index surfaces still show old versions or disabled state
12. Attempt a real Tavily call:

```bash
openclaw infer web search --provider tavily --limit 3 --query "OpenClaw 2026.7.1 release notes" --json
```

13. It fails with missing credential error, even though Tavily was previously configured:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

14. Inspect current config vs backup:
   - `tools.web.search.provider` is still `tavily`
   - but `plugins.entries.tavily` is gone
   - and `tavily` is missing from `plugins.allow`
   - backup config still contains the Tavily API key subtree
15. Manually restore the missing config and allowlist entries, restart gateway, rerun the direct search test
16. Tavily search succeeds, but some status surfaces can still report stale install/version drift

### Expected behavior

- A plugin install metadata conflict should not permanently block startup without a supported convergence path.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` should either resolve the conflict or provide a deterministic repair path.
- Manual uninstall/reinstall of one conflicting plugin should not silently remove config/allowlist/credential subtrees for other working plugins.
- If a plugin capability is actually working again, status surfaces should converge and stop reporting stale drift.
- The combined repair path should be idempotent.

### Actual behavior

- Gateway readiness is blocked by a plugin install metadata conflict.
- `doctor --fix` does not converge the state.
- Manual plugin reinstall is required to recover gateway readiness.
- Another plugin (`tavily`) can lose its config entry, allowlist membership, and API-key subtree during the repair sequence.
- After manual config restoration, the capability works again, but some status/index views still report old version drift or disabled state.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

macOS arm64

### Install method

npm/Homebrew global install

### Model

MiniMax-M3 (not material to the bug)

### Provider / routing chain

- `minimax-portal` for agent runs
- `tavily` for managed web search
- `openclaw-weixin` channel configured

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway managed via macOS LaunchAgent
- external plugins involved in the repro: `openclaw-weixin`, `deepseek`, `tavily`
- Tavily was previously configured and functioning before repair

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

Representative blocking log:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

Representative post-repair Tavily failure:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

Representative successful direct Tavily test only after manual config restoration:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "web.search",
  "provider": "tavily"
}
```

State observations during recovery:
- `plugins.entries.tavily` missing from current config
- `tavily` missing from `plugins.allow`
- backup config still contained Tavily `webSearch.apiKey`
- direct capability call worked again only after restoring both config entry and allowlist
- some status surfaces still reported stale Tavily version/install drift after the capability was already working

### Impact and severity

High.

This can leave an upgraded install in a state where:
- gateway will not start
- official repair does not converge state
- user must manually inspect config/state internals
- plugin credentials/config can be silently dropped during recovery
- status surfaces remain misleading even after functional recovery

### Additional information

This seems related to, but not fully covered by, existing plugin metadata conflict/state-drift issues such as:
- #97563
- #97768
- #90418
- #107727

What seems unique here is the full chain:
- plugin metadata conflict blocks startup
- doctor cannot clear it
- manual conflicting-plugin reinstall restores gateway
- another plugin then loses config/allowlist/credentials
- capability works again only after manual config restoration
- status/index can still drift after successful functional recovery

A robust fix likely needs all of the following:
- a deterministic source of truth for external plugin install state
- safe, idempotent reconciliation between legacy install index, SQLite state, config entries, and allowlist
- repair tooling that can restore plugin config references without silently dropping unrelated plugin credentials
- status surfaces that reflect actual loaded/working capability state after recovery
